title: edikt governance sidecar (v2 — multi-anchor)
description: The <artifact>.edikt.yaml sidecar co-located next to a governance artifact (ADR, invariant, guideline). v2 replaces v1's singular source_excerpt with source_excerpts[], an ordered list of 1..N anchors per directive. The v1 shape could only record ONE span of prose per directive, so a rule whose meaning is established across separate sentences — a Decision line naming a thing and a later paragraph defining it — had nowhere to put the second span. Extraction resolved that by dropping context or by splitting one rule into fragments that each lost the other's meaning. That is a schema-shaped hole, not a prompt defect, and no amount of extractor tuning closes it. Compile reads sidecars verbatim and never mutates the parent .md. source_hash, agent_prompt_version and directives_hash remain forbidden by additionalProperties.
$comment: v2 — source_excerpts[] replaces source_excerpt. The singular key is NOT accepted as an alias: additionalProperties:false rejects it, and the Go loader reports it by name so a half-migrated sidecar fails loudly instead of validating with zero anchors. Migration is bin/edikt migrate --to-v2.

schema_version.description: Sidecar schema version. v2 denotes the multi-anchor shape: directives[] and prohibitions[] carry source_excerpts[] (1..N) instead of v1's singular source_excerpt. A v1 reader cannot interpret a v2 sidecar and must refuse it rather than silently reading zero anchors.

topic.description: Kebab-case topic identifier used to group directives across artifacts during compile. 1–40 characters, must start with a lowercase letter, may contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

path.description: Relative path (from the project root) to the parent .md artifact this sidecar describes. Validated by /edikt:doctor — a sidecar whose path doesn't resolve is reported as orphaned.

body_digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the parent .md body after whitespace normalization, recorded at extraction time. Powers the BODY DRIFT signal: when this differs from the recomputed digest, prose changed that extraction never saw, so the sidecar may be INCOMPLETE — distinct from ANCHOR DRIFT, where a recorded quote no longer matches and the sidecar is WRONG. This is NOT the forbidden source_hash field: that field was a fast-path substitute for checking, where a divergence between recorded and computed values was the DEFECT. Here divergence is the PRODUCT — the field exists precisely to be compared and to disagree. source_hash, agent_prompt_version and directives_hash remain forbidden. Optional: sidecars written before this field existed have no baseline and MUST be reported as UNMEASURED, never as unchanged.

items.description: Lowercase signal phrase. Indexed for search and for the benchmark attack corpus; topic routing is the approved registry description, not this set when a task matches the signal.

signals.description: Lowercase, deduplicated keyword/phrase signals that route work to this artifact.

paths.description: v1.1 (optional). File-glob patterns scoping where this artifact's directives apply (e.g. 'tools/edikt/**/*.go', 'templates/hooks/**/*.sh'). Glob syntax is doublestar/v4 compatible. Validated as non-empty strings at parse time; full glob-syntax validation deferred to gov:compile.

scope.description: v1.1 (optional). Lifecycle phases during which this artifact's directives are surfaced. Closed enum: planning | design | implementation | review. ADR Decision blocks default to [design, implementation, review]; INV Statements default to [implementation, review]; ADR architectural prohibitions default to [planning, design, review].

text.description: MUST NOT directive synthesised from a rejected option. Same shape as directives[].text.

derived_from.description: Provenance hint for the prohibition (e.g., 'rejected_option_b'). Optional; auditability only — not used by compile.

verify.description: Optional shell command that returns exit 0 when the prohibition is honored, non-zero when it is violated. Run via `bin/edikt verify gov <ID>`. The completion-evidence discipline refuses to declare success when any verify fails. Omit when no mechanical check is possible — the field stays absent, not empty.

verify_kind.description: v1.2 (optional). The enforcement medium of the verify command. behavioral = runs code and asserts a property; tooling = invokes a stable external tool with a fixed rule ID; structural = grep/file-presence over content (only valid when the prohibition's property is itself structural). Layer-independent — applies to every verify: command regardless of which sidecar carries it.

intent.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line semantic claim of the prohibition, generator-neutral. Consumed by the L2 governance-verifier instead of the raw text. Must read as the assertion without referencing implementation symbols the generator controls.

falsifying_observation.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line description of what a violation looks like. Used by the L2 verifier to decide PASS/FAIL/NEEDS_REVIEW. Required (non-null) when verify_kind == behavioral; Phase B compile enforces this conditional-required constraint.

human_approved_at.description: v1.2 (optional). RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of human approval. Required by CONTRACT (non-null) for verify_kind == behavioral, but NOT enforced at compile — the check is deferred to a later phase (AC-4.3), so an unapproved behavioral verify compiles today. Set by `bin/edikt sidecar approve`.

positive_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits 0 when the directive's behavioral property holds.

negative_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits non-zero when the directive's behavioral property is violated.

line_start.description: 1-indexed line in the parent .md where this anchor's source text begins.

line_end.description: 1-indexed line where this anchor's source text ends. Must be >= line_start; range-vs-file-length is checked by doctor and the compile resync pass, not by JSON Schema.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the parent .md spanning line_start..line_end. Anchor drift compares this against the live prose; a mismatch means the sidecar is WRONG (distinct from body drift, where it may merely be INCOMPLETE).

role.description: v2 (optional). What this anchor contributes to the directive. The first anchor is conventionally the statement; later anchors typically carry the definition or scope that the statement alone does not. Advisory metadata — grading and drift treat all anchors alike.

source_excerpts.description: v2. Ordered anchors (1..N) grounding this prohibition in the parent .md. At least one is required: a prohibition with zero anchors is ungrounded and cannot be drift-checked. Multiple anchors exist so a rule established across separate spans of prose can record every span it depends on, instead of discarding all but one.

needs_review.description: v2 (optional; absent means false). Set by the extractor when a candidate falls in one of the two residual classes the calibrated content-scope rule provably cannot settle from inside a single artifact: (a) an unattributed cross-artifact restatement — another artifact's rule restated here without citation, indistinguishable from an original rule under extraction's single-artifact isolation; (b) an aspirational obligation in a Consequences section, which has the grammar of a rule and the position of an outcome. It is a REVIEW FLAG, never a suppression: the directive still compiles and still binds, and it is marked for a human to confirm or remove. Routing these to review is the alternative to the two silent failures — extracting them unmarked, or dropping them unmentioned.

actor_scope.description: v2 (optional; absent means false). ADR-065. Set on a directive/prohibition whose subject is an edikt-internal automated operation (the compilation pipeline, gov:compile, migrate, upgrade) rather than file content a human edit could violate. hook match's write-time MUST-grade selection excludes actor_scope: true entries unconditionally — that channel only ever observes Claude-Code-mediated Edit/Write calls, which the Go-internal pipeline operations never make, so delivering these as PreToolUse bounces is noise with no enforcement value through this specific surface. Excluded entries still compile and still render in ambient/topic-file surfaces; only write-time PreToolUse delivery is affected. A per-directive, reviewed, deliberate opt-in — never inferred by the extractor.

prohibitions.description: v1.1 (optional). MUST NOT directives synthesised from rejected '## Considered Options' (ADRs only). Each entry MUST have a verifiable source_excerpt pointing to a Cons: bullet or rejected-option body in the parent .md. Extractor never invents a prohibition that is not literally present in rejected-option text (see Phase 2 Rule C in templates/agents/sidecar-extractor.md).

manual_directives.description: User-authored rules preserved across sidecar regenerations. Always included in the effective rule set. Never overwritten by sidecar-extractor.

suppressed_directives.description: Auto-directives the user rejected. Subtracted from directives[] at gov:compile time. Never overwritten by sidecar-extractor.

reminders.description: Pre-action reminders aggregated into governance.md ## Reminders. Format: 'Before {action} → {check} (ref: ID)'. Extracted from ## Confirmation (ADRs) and ## Enforcement (INVs).

oneOf.description: Legacy bare-string form. Verification checklist item in '[ ] {what to check} (ref: ID)' format. Aggregated into governance.md ## Verification Checklist. Human-readable only — no programmatic check.

text.description: Verification checklist item — same content as the bare-string form.

verify.description: Optional shell command that runs the checklist item mechanically. Exit 0 = pass. Used by `bin/edikt verify gov <ID>` to enforce the completion-evidence discipline.

verification.description: Verification checklist items aggregated into governance.md ## Verification Checklist. Two forms accepted (oneOf): bare string (legacy), or {text, verify?} object (preferred for new entries — carries the executable check that proves the item).

migration_preserved.description: v0.6.x two-phase upgrade baseline (Phase A of the migration-as-cleanup refactor). Populated by `edikt migrate sidecars --apply` with the verbatim content of the legacy [edikt:directives:start] block; consumed by the sidecar-extractor agent on the first compile after migration, then stripped from the sidecar by Phase B (compile). Sidecars in steady state do NOT carry this field. Its presence is a structural signal that the artifact has just been migrated and is awaiting its first canonical extraction.

schema_detected.description: What the migrator detected the legacy sentinel block to be. Audit-only; extractor uses the structured content below regardless of detection.

directives.description: Legacy directive strings (the sentinel block's directives:[] list, verbatim). Extractor MUST include each of these in its output, verbatim, then synthesize additional directives from prose that aren't already covered.

manual_directives.description: Legacy manual_directives:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the manual_directives field.

suppressed_directives.description: Legacy suppressed_directives:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the suppressed_directives field.

reminders.description: Legacy reminders:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the reminders field.

verification.description: Legacy verification:[] list, verbatim. Extractor MUST output these in the verification field.

topic.description: Legacy topic if present (v0.5.x sentinels). Extractor MAY use this as a hint when synthesizing the canonical topic field.

signals.description: Legacy signals if present (v0.5.x sentinels). Extractor MAY use this as a hint when synthesizing the canonical signals field.

text.description: The directive sentence as it will appear in compiled governance, ≤ 500 characters. Includes its own ref tail (e.g., '(ref: ADR-NNN)'). 500 chars is deliberate headroom — natural-language rules with multiple clauses routinely run 200–280 chars; rules that would exceed it should be split.

verify.description: Optional shell command that returns exit 0 when the directive holds, non-zero when it is violated. Run via `bin/edikt verify gov <ID>`. The completion-evidence discipline refuses to declare success when any verify fails. Omit when no mechanical check is possible — the field stays absent, not empty.

verify_kind.description: v1.2 (optional). The enforcement medium of the verify command. behavioral = runs code and asserts a property; tooling = invokes a stable external tool with a fixed rule ID; structural = grep/file-presence over content (only valid when the directive's property is itself structural, e.g., 'no go.mod at root'). The mechanism-quality axis; layer-independent and harness-independent. Phase B compile enforces: if `verify` is set, `verify_kind` MUST also be set.

intent.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line semantic claim of the directive, generator-neutral. Consumed by the L2 governance-verifier instead of the raw `text`. Must read as the directive's assertion without referencing implementation symbols the generator controls.

falsifying_observation.description: v1.2 (optional). One-line description of what a violation looks like. Used by the L2 verifier to decide PASS/FAIL/NEEDS_REVIEW. Required (non-null) when verify_kind == behavioral; Phase B compile enforces this conditional-required constraint.

human_approved_at.description: v1.2 (optional). RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of human approval. Required by CONTRACT (non-null) for verify_kind == behavioral, but NOT enforced at compile — the check is deferred to a later phase (AC-4.3), so an unapproved behavioral verify compiles today. Set by `bin/edikt sidecar approve`; the tier-1 wrapper captures the user's decision via Claude Code's AskUserQuestion before dispatching the tier-2 binary.

positive_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits 0 when the directive's behavioral property holds.

negative_fixture_path.description: Path to a script that exits non-zero when the directive's behavioral property is violated.

line_start.description: 1-indexed line in the parent .md where this anchor's source text begins.

line_end.description: 1-indexed line where this anchor's source text ends. Must be >= line_start; range-vs-file-length is checked by doctor and the compile resync pass, not by JSON Schema.

Set on a directive/prohibition whose subject is an edikt-internal automated operation (the compilation pipeline, gov:compile, migrate, upgrade) rather than file content a human edit could violate. hook match's write-time MUST-grade selection excludes actor_scope: true entries unconditionally — that channel only ever observes Claude-Code-mediated Edit/Write calls, which the Go-internal pipeline operations never make, so delivering these as PreToolUse bounces is noise with no enforcement value through this specific surface. directives.description: Directive list extracted from the parent .md. May be empty (an artifact with no enforceable directives is reported by /edikt:doctor as a warning, not an error). Note: line_end ≥ line_start and line_end ≤ parent_file_line_count are enforced by /edikt:doctor and the compile resync pass — JSON Schema 2020-12 has no standard cross-property comparator. v1.2 conditional-required constraints are declared here but enforced at Phase B compile time rather than at schema-validation time, because JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot express conditional-required across siblings cleanly. Two of the three are enforced today: verify_kind when verify is set, and falsifying_observation when verify_kind == behavioral. The third — human_approved_at when verify_kind == behavioral — is required by contract but NOT checked, its enforcement deliberately deferred to a later phase (AC-4.3).

proposed_paths.description: v2 (optional). Paths globs PROPOSED by extraction but not yet human-approved — they do not scope anything until promoted into paths[] via `bin/edikt sidecar approve --kind paths`. Kept separate from paths[] so an inferred guess can never silently become an enforced scope; an unapproved proposal is unmeasured, not authoritative.

glob.description: doublestar/v4-compatible glob. Catch-alls are rejected at the schema level: a glob matching everything scopes nothing and silently re-creates the ambient-load problem this release exists to remove.

evidence.description: Why this glob was proposed — the prose or filename observation it came from. Required: a proposal without evidence cannot be reviewed, only rubber-stamped.

matched_example.description: Optional. A real repo path this glob matched at proposal time. The requirement that a proposal match at least one existing file is enforced by the Go validator, which can stat the tree; JSON Schema cannot.

proposed_removals.description: v2 (optional). Paths globs PROPOSED for removal from an existing paths[] scope, but not yet human-approved — they continue to enforce until promoted (removed) via `bin/edikt sidecar approve --kind paths`. Unlike proposed_paths (extractor-generated), a removal is a reviewed, human-initiated narrowing: nothing infers that a glob is over-broad. At approval time the ceremony computes a coverage preview (files that would lose this artifact's directives) and REFUSES outright if any lost file is literally named in the sidecar's own directive/prohibition text — a narrowing that un-governs a file the text mentions is a defect, not a judgment call.

glob.description: The glob to remove from paths[]. Must currently be present in paths[]; the ceremony refuses removal of a glob that isn't there rather than silently no-op.

evidence.description: Why this glob is over-broad relative to what the directive text actually supports — the prose evidence a reviewer can check the coverage preview against.

proposed_topic_description.description: v2 (optional, transient). The extractor's SUGGESTED one-line registry description for this sidecar's topic — the 'extracted' half of the extracted-then-approved ceremony. It is not a description: no surface renders it, and it reaches .edikt/topics.yaml only through `bin/edikt sidecar approve --kind topic-description`, which stamps a hash over the exact bytes a human approved. Routed out to .edikt/state/pending-topic-descriptions/<topic>.yaml and stripped from the sidecar before steady state, exactly like proposed_paths and migration_preserved.

paths_approval.description: v2 (optional). Receipt for a paths approval performed through `bin/edikt sidecar approve --kind paths`. Without it, a sidecar whose paths went through the ceremony is BYTE-IDENTICAL to one where an extractor wrote paths[] directly — so no gate can tell an approved scope from a declared one, and AC-4.4's 'approved fields survive regeneration byte-intact' asserts a property the data cannot express. Recorded as F-004.

approved_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the approval.

globs_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the sorted approved globs, newline-joined. Content-addressed on purpose: a receipt carrying only a timestamp would still validate after someone edited paths[] by hand afterwards, which is exactly the case it exists to catch.
